title: Ubisoft cuts 166 jobs at Montreal and Quebec City video game studios

image.caption: The Ubisoft building in Quebec is seen on May 7, 2024. The company said on Thursday it was laying off 166 employees at its Quebec City and Montreal offices. (Jacques Boissinot/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Ubisoft's head of public relations told Radio-Canada that the cuts impacted production teams as well as some workers who support production. The cuts aren't the first this year for Ubisoft's Canadian workforce — nor for the broader video game industry.
Cuts impact less than 4% of Canadian Ubisoft workforce, spokesperson says
Ubisoft is laying off 166 staff at its Montreal and Quebec City studios, the company confirmed on Thursday.

In a statement to Radio-Canada, Ubisoft's head of public relations, Antoine Leduc-Labelle, said 128 positions in Montreal and 38 in Quebec City were eliminated, impacting less than four per cent of the company's Canadian workforce.
The layoffs impact production teams, as well as some workers that support production, according to the company spokesperson.
The company said changing production needs required them to make the cuts, "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."
Those affected will receive resources like severance pay and career transition resources, the company said.

"We highly value the contribution of these teams and recognize the impact this decision may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them throughout this process with care and respect," a Ubisoft spokesperson said in a statement in French.

The layoffs aren't the first for Ubisoft's Canadian workforce this year, nor for the broader video game industry. After investments and team sizes boomed during the pandemic, the industry has shrunk and jobs have been cut at many game-making firms.
Ubisoft shuttered its Winnipeg studio in June, impacting 65 employees there, four years after the firm said it planned to triple its Winnipeg workforce by 2030.

Quebec video game industry in limbo as studios cut back

blocks.text: In January, the French videogame maker closed up shop in Halifax, eliminating just over 70 jobs. The layoffs came just after the Halifax workforce formed the company's first union in North America, though the company said the layoffs were a result of cost-cutting and efficiency measures, adding the restructuring predated the efforts to unionize.
Just last month, Electronic Arts shut down its Edmonton-based game studio BioWare, slashing 50 jobs at BioWare specifically and 400 in total.
